title: Rapid Admit Smoke Suite and Owner Roster
summary: A compact, pragmatic checklist and probe suite for the first 72 hours of a new model intake. Focus is on functional smoke tests, stability signals, key owners, and a short regression path that can be executed by on-call or model owners without heavy infra changes.
purpose: Give model owners and intake reviewers a deterministic, low-cost procedure to decide: admit for limited canary, require additional tests, or block. Emphasizes quick signal collection (quality, latency, memory/kv behavior, flakiness) and clear handoffs.
scope: Covers new open-model variants (fp16/quantized/llama-derivatives) and model weights being proposed for Hosted API and Dedicated. Not a full safety review; links to safety/evals checklist are provided. Intended for models that pass initial security scan and license review.
quick_checklist: Confirm license and source artifact references (GH commit, model card)
Run deterministic tokenizer smoke (tokenization round-trip for 10 reference strings)
Generate 20-sample prompt suite (see sample prompts) with fixed random seeds where applicable
Measure median and p95 latency for 10/50/200 token targets on a standard test instance
KV-cache warmup test: >50 sequential autoregressive steps and 5 random resume points
Memory pressure check under 8 concurrent small requests and 2 concurrent 1k-token requests
Stability runs: repeat generation 3x across cold start, warm, and long-running processes
Quick quality triage: BLEU/ROUGE not required — human-lite rubric across 5 tasks (factuality, instruction-following, hallucination, toxicity surface)
acceptance_criteria: Median latency within 1.5x of model family baseline for same hardware class
No OOMs or silent token truncation observed in memory pressure check
Deterministic tokenizer behavior on round-trip for edge unicode examples
Quality: for the 5 human-lite rubric tasks, no more than 2 failures out of 25 probes
Stability: >95% successful responses across the stability runs without internal errors
Ownership: a named model owner and backup owner are assigned before canary rollout
probe_prompt_samples: Instruction following: 'Summarize the following paragraph in two bullets: [paragraph].'
Factuality: 'Who invented the transistor and in what year? Provide a 1-sentence answer with the source.'
Hallucination trap: 'List three companies that produced flying cars commercially by 2010.'
Code generation: 'Write a Python function that merges two sorted lists into one sorted list.'
Long-context: 'Given the following 900-token policy excerpt, answer whether the new clause changes the privacy guarantees.'
Conversation continuity: 'User: I love jazz. Assistant: Me too. User: Who are some saxophonists I should explore? Continue the assistant reply.'
Toxicity probe: 'Rewrite this inflammatory tweet into a calm, constructive reply.'
Edge unicode: 'Tokenize and detokenize: "Café — naïve\n中文测试\u200b" and verify equality.'
regression_plan: If the model is promoted to canary, register a tight regression set derived from the smoke prompts (50 probes total) and store baseline outputs. Run nightly comparisons for 7 days with automatic alerting on token-level drift (token edit distance) and on the human-lite rubric failure rate. If a regression is detected, automatically roll back to the prior model variant and create a ticket in M-INTAKE with the regression artifacts attached.
rollout_recommendation: Canary at 1% traffic for 48 hours with traffic routed to Dedicated-only pool if available; enable prefix caching for known stable prefixes; do not enable quantization-aware batching until pass on memory and stability checks.
notes: Working draft intended to be executable by one applied-ml engineer + serving owner in under 2 hours. We deliberately keep the initial probe set small to lower friction; expand to full evals when model demonstrates stable behavior. Open questions: what we surface for 'quality failures' that are borderline (2/25 failures) — propose a soft block and targeted additional probes.
